rows.currentScript: The card gives you “cup” to build on. Bring in “board” and you get cupboard. Plate and spoon seem to fit, though no word forms there.
rows.whyRewrite: "The card gives you “cup” to build on." names a card the question is not shown to have; the stem is a prompt with one word, and no card can be checked on the screen. The rest (cupboard; plate and spoon form no word) is correct.

rows.currentScript: Begin with the single word “grand”. Stick “mother” on and you build grandmother. House and old sound close, yet each stays a made-up word.
rows.whyRewrite: "House and old sound close, yet each stays a made-up word." says house and old are made-up words. They are real words; only grandhouse and grandold are not. The working (grandmother) is correct.

rows.currentScript: Begin with the base word “pan”. Add “cake” to make pancake. Pot sounds sensible, but it never joins into one word.
rows.whyRewrite: Fault is in the QUESTION: fry gives a second defensible answer (panfry is a closed dictionary word, and frypan also exists, since the prompt does not fix the order). The script also leaves fry out entirely and says only "Pot sounds sensible, but it never joins into one word."

rows.currentScript: The first part reads “sea”. Add “weed” and the word becomes seaweed. Seaweed is a real plant. Sand and wave fit the idea, but they never join up.
rows.whyRewrite: "Seaweed is a real plant." is not a true claim: seaweed is algae, not a plant. The sentence adds nothing to the method and should be cut. seaweed itself and the wrong options (sand, wave) are handled correctly.

rows.currentScript: Look at “farm” at the start. Join “yard” to it and you make farmyard. Farmyard is a real place. Field and barn sound close, yet each stays a made-up word.
rows.whyRewrite: "Field and barn sound close, yet each stays a made-up word." says field and barn are made-up words. They are real words; only farmfield and farmbarn are not. farmyard is correct.
